extra.message: The `fragment` query parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 template source string which is then compiled and rendered. cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The privilege decision is made entirely from a client-supplied `ops_badge` cookie or `x-ops-badge` header. Authorization must be derived from authoritative server-side identity (the session user's role), not from request-controlled input.

extra.message: `secret_key` falls back to the hardcoded literal `dev-only-change-me-support-desk` when SECRET_KEY is unset. If the app is deployed without the env var, anyone knowing this public default can forge a session cookie for any `uid`, i.e. full authentication bypass as support_admin, and forge API keys.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: MD5 is used to digest a user-supplied phrase. MD5 is collision-prone and, being fast and unsalted, is trivially reversible for low-entropy inputs via rainbow tables. It must not be used for any security-relevant digest.

extra.message: The login endpoint performs an unbounded number of password verifications per client. There is no per-account lockout, no failed-attempt counter on the User model (app/models.py:88-105), no rate-limiting middleware in app/main.py, and no rate-limiting dependency in requirements.txt. An attacker can mount unlimited online credential-stuffing/brute-force attacks against any account.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Neither the password-reset request nor the reset-confirm endpoint is rate limited or throttled. `/password-reset/confirm` looks a user up directly by the HMAC of a client-supplied token, so an attacker can submit unlimited token guesses, and `/password-reset/request` can be abused for unbounded reset-mail generation against enumerated addresses.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Only successful logins are written to the audit log (line 37). Failed authentication attempts raise a 401 and return without any `log_audit` call, and there is no global middleware or exception handler in app/main.py that records them. The same gap exists for failed API-key authentication (app/deps.py:55-56) and for authorization denials (app/deps.py:44, app/deps.py:79). Credential-guessing and privilege-probing campaigns therefore leave no durable security-audit trail.

cwe: CWE-778: Insufficient Logging

extra.message: Logout only deletes the client cookie; the itsdangerous-signed session token (app/security.py:27-36) is stateless and carries no server-side revocation list, so a token captured before logout stays valid for the full 8-hour `session_max_age_seconds`. `current_user` (app/deps.py:32-34) also accepts the token via an `Authorization: Bearer` header, so a stolen token remains usable after the user believes they have signed out.
